violated_contract: A get-or-create keyed on a person's display name must find the existing person under the same name equality the rest of the system uses: renames dedupe aliases by casefolded, whitespace-collapsed names, and the live owner check casefolds too. find_person_by_name ran only an exact Firestore name == query, which is case-sensitive, so a person saved as "alice" or "Mcdonald" was never found from "Alice" or "McDonald". POST /v1/users/people, speaker tag-card names and live explicit introductions then created a duplicate person, and copula introductions and sync text naming left the speaker unresolved.
canonical_prevention: Keep the exact indexed query as the fast path and, only on a miss, compare normalized_person_alias(name).casefold() against the owner's active people, an owner-scoped collection read that needs no new index. Pin case variants with a fake whose == filter compares exactly, as Firestore does.
